title: One Voice, Many Channels Explained Simply | Marketing Management Ep 28
description:
Laddoo Lab's pack says tiffin sweet, Dev's post says gym snack, and Arjun calls it a festive treat. Mrs. Rao sees all three and remembers none of them. In this animated lesson we use Laddoo Lab, a millet laddoo brand from Bengaluru, to understand integrated marketing communications (IMC).

You will see Philip Kotler and Gary Armstrong's definition of IMC, where the idea came from (Don Schultz of Northwestern University co-wrote the first IMC textbook in 1993), and the five tools of the promotion mix: advertising, sales promotion, personal selling, public relations, and direct and digital marketing. Then we watch one week of Mrs. Rao's life twice: the old way with mixed messages, and the integrated way where every channel says the same thing and her memory builds until she buys. Zoya plans the campaign in four steps (audience, goal, message, tools), and we see one message, one look, the right tool for each job and checking results at work today in a phone maker, a bank, an airline and a food delivery app. We also look at the human side honestly: one voice is hard when teams pull different ways and can get boring, so the lesson is to keep one voice but find fresh ways to say it.

This is Episode 28 of our Marketing Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.
